title: Strings
learn: immutability in Python, `''.join` vs `+=`, char codes (`ord`/`chr`), counting chars, splitting/parsing
hook: String questions look easy and hide traps: an innocent `s += c` in a loop is O(n²), and parsing questions like atoi are all about edge cases. Interviewers use them to see how carefully you handle details.

explain.prompt: Explain why building a string with `+=` in a loop can be slow in Python, and what you'd do instead.
keyPoints: Python strings are immutable, so every change creates a new string
`s += c` can copy the whole string each time, O(n²) over n appends
collect pieces in a list and call "".join once: O(n) total
reading `s[i]` is still O(1), like any array
